stallings.title: Computer Organization and Architecture: Designing for Performance

ph.title: Computer Organization and Design: The Hardware/Software Interface (MIPS edition)
ph.authors: David A. Patterson and John L. Hennessy

computer-evolution-and-performance.why: CPU time, CPI, clock rate and MIPS with worked comparisons like the 2020/21 paper.

organization-architecture-and-instructio.read: Chapters 1–3: Basic Concepts; Performance Issues; A Top-Level View of Computer Function
organization-architecture-and-instructio.why: Organization versus architecture, the von Neumann model and the instruction cycle the course book follows.

registers-and-number-representation.read: Chapters 9 and 10: Number Systems; Computer Arithmetic
registers-and-number-representation.why: Number bases, sign-magnitude, two's complement and floating point.

cpu-alu-and-addressing-modes.why: Register organization, instruction formats with three-, two-, one- and zero-address examples, and addressing modes as in the course book.

risc-cisc-and-parallelism.read: Chapter 8, Section 8-8: Reduced Instruction Set Computer; Chapter 9: Pipeline and Vector Processing (Flynn)
risc-cisc-and-parallelism.why: CISC and RISC characteristics, Berkeley RISC I and register windows, and Flynn's classification.

pipelining.why: The five-stage MIPS pipeline, hazards, stalls and forwarding asked in the 2020/21 paper.

memory-hierarchy-and-cache.read: Chapters 4 and 5: Cache Memory; Internal Memory
memory-hierarchy-and-cache.why: The memory hierarchy, cache mapping, SRAM, DRAM and ROM types.
